newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela downsizes FIV's privatization unit.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela downsizes FIV's privatization unit.

text.p: The head of privatization at Venezuela's privatization agency, the Venezuelan Investment Fund (FIV) has been fired as part of wider plans to downsize the FIV and shrink Venezuela's bloated public sector, FIV officials told Reuters.
The head of the FIV's privatization unit, Carlos Chacon, two other top level managers and 11 middle level managers, have so far been dismissed, said Oscar Lopez Colima, FIV's head of Human Resources.
"We're looking towards the future and working on ways to restructure the FIV and streamline it. Currently we're a very rigid organization," he told Reuters.

Chacon, who was asked 15 days ago by FIV president Alberto Poletto for his resignation, told Reuters that he nevertheless expected privatization of Venezuela's Corporacion Venezolana de Guayana (CVG) industrial complex to go ahead successfully.
"The slated aluminum and Sidor privatizations are already well advanced and I'm sure they'll be successful," he said.
"The critical part will be the forthcoming congressional discussions. Congress will have to be convinced that their sale is a plus for Venezuela."
Government officials are due to firm up sale contract details with bankers in New York this week.
Other FIV sources, who asked to remain anonymous, said the FIV's restructuring comes on the heels of the successful sale of national telephone company CANTV late last year.
But rumors that up to 200 people will be dismissed, from the FIV's current staff of 400, are completely false, a source said.

"After CANTV's sale and, we hope, CVG's, the FIV has to find a new role for itself ... We don't have much left to privatize, so it may be managing the Debt Rescue Fund, or a return to the Fund's original charter, strategic investment," said the source.
Plans to establish the Debt Rescue Fund, which will be used to pay off debt with privatization proceeds, is pending congressional approval.
The CVG's four aluminum firms as well as steel producer Sidor are due to be privatized before the second half of the year.
